synthesis.body: To show a subprocess never reaches the network, blocking egress and checking the exit code only proves it tolerates failure. On macOS use sandbox-exec with '(deny network-outbound (with send-signal SIGKILL))' so any attempt is fatal: completion then proves no attempt from any code path, including compiled extensions a Python-level socket tracer cannot see. Validate the instrument before trusting it -- trivial process survives, IP-literal connect is killed (a DNS-only block lets hardcoded IPs through), DNS-based urlopen is killed, the same request succeeds unsandboxed. '(with report)' is rejected on a deny action and sandbox denials did not reach the unified log on Darwin 25.5, so log scraping is not a substitute. Does not port to Linux CI: use a network namespace or seccomp filter, with its own negative control.

title: Prove a process makes no network request with kill-on-egress, and run the negative control first
